prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The best single probe was enabling timing-driven net weighting (c007, +0.423). Building on c004's looser area balance, the strongest available lever in the shown chunks is to make the partitioner's area-balance repair less disruptive to the timing-critical clustering: raise `area_balance_error` further (0.15 -> 0.20) so fewer macros are force-flipped away from their embedding cluster, preserving the wirelength-aware tier assignment that reduces cross-tier detours and TNS.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.039 robust(mean-std)=-0.020 min_case=-0.013 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.059 dWNS=-0.5% dTNS=+10.6% overflow~90
  bp-ng45: score=-0.013 dWNS=-5.3% dTNS=+1.4% overflow~123
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.007 dWNS=+1.7% dTNS=-1.9% overflow~132
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis did not hold: raising `area_balance_error` to 0.20 gave only +0.039 total and a negative robust score (-0.020), with two of three cases slightly negative. Ariane improved (score +0.059, dTNS +10.6%), consistent with fewer forced macro flips preserving timing-critical clustering, but bp-ng45 and bp_fe-ng45 regressed (dWNS -5.3% and +1.7% respectively), suggesting the looser balance hurts wirelength/overflow on those designs. Next step: sweep intermediate values (0.16–0.18) or apply the looser balance selectively per design, since the benefit appears case-dependent rather than universal.
